name: Shadows of the Praxeum
throughline_question: What does loyalty cost when every allegiance demands a different piece of you?

sensory: the perpetual humidity of Yavin 4 — even the duracrete sweats at midday
the smell of jungle rot mixed with ozone where the temple's ancient power conduits still leak
the dawn chorus of Whyren-fliers above the canopy — like bells underwater
the way the temple stone is warm at midday and cold by an hour after sunset, as if it remembers a sun that no longer reaches it
the reflective coral of the inner Massassi corridors that brightens when Force-sensitive students walk past — only fractionally, only to those watching
the quiet hiss of Tionne's recording crystals warming up in the archive at dusk
ritual: the morning meditation chime — three notes, the third half a tone flat by Luke's deliberate tuning
the meal-share custom Luke instituted — students take turns naming a small thing they were grateful for that day
the lighting of the perimeter glow-lanterns at sundown by the youngest student present
the silent walk Tionne makes around the archive's perimeter every night before sealing the door
the noon maintenance bell that means everyone stops training long enough to keep the temple habitable
Luke's rule that no student spars twice with the same partner until they have eaten together once
objects: Tionne's recordings — small crystalline data wafers shelved alphabetically by the name of the Jedi they describe
salvaged kyber crystals from the lower Massassi levels, each one humming at a different almost-audible frequency
the Praxeum's perimeter glow-lanterns, each one carved with the symbol of the student whose responsibility it is to maintain it
the cracked obsidian disc Luke keeps on his desk — a fragment from the Death Star's debris field, kept as a discipline against forgetting
the practice remotes Luke salvaged from a Clone Wars-era training ship, still bearing scuff marks from earlier Padawans
a hand-drawn temple map in the student common room, wrong in three places and corrected by three different people
language: students address Luke as 'Master Luke' only in formal contexts — otherwise simply 'Luke' (a deliberate break from the old Order's hierarchy)
Tionne uses 'lessons' instead of 'lectures' — a deliberate framing choice
the older students have begun greeting one another with 'May the Force breathe' — a phrase Luke neither encourages nor stops
Mirialan formality permits the prayer-form 'Ka'thari' (carry it well) when entrusting a difficult task to a friend
support staff call unexplored corridors 'old teeth' because every new passage bites someone eventually
students use 'glow duty' as shorthand for any small responsibility that proves you live here, not just train here
sensory_anchors: The lower temple's sealed-stairway draft — not cold, exactly, but slightly thinner-feeling than the air above, the way a room two days after a death is thinner than a room before

The faint salt-iron taste at the back of the throat after a long meditation in the meditation chamber, which Luke does not explain and which the older students attribute, half-jokingly, to the year before
The high-tower wind, which has its own voice — not howl, not whistle, a low fluted note older students claim only Streen can interpret
rituals: The post-Exar-Kun silence — twelve seconds at the start of the noon meal, not formal, not announced, a habit the senior students kept after the crisis and the new students learn by watching
Kyp Durron's evening repetition: he passes through the colonnade after dinner, alone, walking the same loop he walked the night Luke pulled him back; the students who notice do not comment
significant_objects: A Massassi-stone fragment Luke keeps on his desk, scorched on one face — what's left of a corridor that fell during the Exar Kun crisis, kept as a reminder that walls fail
Tionne's sealed crate at the back of the archive — recent seals, content unspecified to students; senior staff know it holds a Sith holocron she has chosen not to destroy
The wooden shape Streen is whittling — has been the same piece of wood for over a year, somehow never finished, somehow never the same shape twice

allegiances.description: Students of Luke Skywalker's newly founded Jedi Praxeum on Yavin 4, learning to wield the Force in a galaxy that has not yet decided whether the Jedi should exist at all.

character_variants.pitch: A Mirialan student at Luke Skywalker's Jedi Praxeum, drawn to the Force but haunted by the fear that caring too much makes you weak. Your closest friend at the academy is Kira Denn. You share everything. Or so you thought.
character_variants.starting_situation: Three months into training at the Praxeum. The morning meditation session ended with a vision -- Kira's face, overlaid with shadow, a red blade reflected in her eyes. Master Skywalker dismissed it as training noise. It did not feel like noise.
character_variants.voice_baseline: Earnest, precise, occasionally wry. Speaks in complete sentences. Thinks before responding but sometimes the thinking shows. Uses humor to deflect vulnerability. Deeply observant of others, less honest about themselves.
character_variants.background: A Mirialan from Mirial who felt the Force as a child but had no name for it until a New Republic recruiter recognized the signs. Arrived at Yavin 4 six months ago. Bonded immediately with Kira Denn over shared loneliness and a mutual distrust of easy answers.

integration_layer.entry_point: The student has been at the Praxeum for six months, deep enough in training to feel invested but early enough to still be uncertain about belonging.
integration_layer.personal_stakes: If the student reports Kira, they lose the only person who makes the academy feel like home. If they protect Kira, they betray Luke's trust and potentially endanger everyone.

anchor_adaptations.academy_arrival: Participates in morning meditation, senses something wrong through the Force
anchor_adaptations.night_investigation: Follows Kira into the Massassi ruins using Sense
anchor_adaptations.inquisitor_contact: Confronts Malakai through the Force -- feels his training, his pain, his patience
anchor_adaptations.betrayal_crisis: Must decide what to tell Luke about everything
anchor_adaptations.final_convergence: Faces Kira in the temple as the Imperial Remnant attacks

weapons.narrative_note: Built under Luke's guidance from a salvaged crystal. The blade hums low and steady. It feels like an extension of the arm, not a weapon.

special_items.mechanical_effect: Once per session, adds 1 boost die to a Discipline check.
special_items.narrative_note: Hand-carved from Mirialwood. Each bead represents a lesson learned. Three are blank, waiting.

starting_force_powers.name: Sense
starting_force_powers.narrative_capability: Can sense the emotions and intentions of nearby beings. With concentration, can detect danger before it arrives.
starting_force_powers.gm_choice_guidance: Offer sensing choices when the character could read emotions, detect lies, feel danger, or perceive hidden threats. Particularly relevant when interacting with Kira or approaching the Massassi ruins.
starting_force_powers.dark_side_flavor: Dark side Sense is invasive -- not reading but ripping. The emotions come raw and unfiltered. Using it on Kira would feel like a betrayal of trust.

character_variants.protagonist_contradiction: Believes the Force is a gift that should be shared freely, but instinctively hoards knowledge and power to protect those they care about -- especially Kira.
character_variants.pressure_revealed_identity: Under maximum pressure, the student becomes the person who sacrifices their own peace to protect others -- not because it is right, but because they cannot bear to lose anyone else.
character_variants.contradiction_origin: The student's family on Mirial practiced communal Force traditions where gifts were shared openly. But the student watched their older sibling leave to share those gifts with the wider galaxy and never come back. Sharing became synonymous with loss.

depth_card.inner_demon: Fear of inadequacy -- the conviction that they are not strong enough, wise enough, or brave enough to protect the people they love.
depth_card.secret_yearning: To belong somewhere permanently. The Praxeum is the first place that felt like home since Mirial.
depth_card.lesson_not_learned: That you cannot protect people by controlling information. Withholding truth is its own kind of betrayal.
depth_card.worst_act: On Mirial, sensed that their sibling was in danger before they left. Said nothing. The sibling never returned.
depth_card.social_mask: Earnest and slightly self-deprecating. Plays the diligent student who asks good questions. Hides the depth of their attachment to Kira.
depth_card.under_pressure: Becomes controlling -- gathers information, makes plans, tries to manage situations alone.
depth_card.worldview: The galaxy is full of people who need help and institutions that fail them. The Force is the bridge.
depth_card.moral_line: Will not sacrifice an innocent to protect a guilty friend. But the line between innocent and guilty is where the real torture lives.

character_variants.pitch: Clovis Beryl, a human Sentinel/Shadow in his early twenties, survived an Imperial execution order because smugglers pulled him out through the cracks. At Luke's Praxeum he is learning that the Force is not just survival instinct -- and that trust may be harder than stealth.
character_variants.starting_situation: Clovis has been at the Praxeum for five weeks. The first days were practical: where the generators sit, which stairs echo, who checks the perimeter lanterns, how long Luke waits before correcting a student's stance. Kira Denn became his first friend after catching him mapping blind spots in the temple corridors and asking, without judgment, where the best hiding place was. Now daily life is beginning to feel almost believable -- morning meditation, shared meals, sparring drills, archive chores -- when Kira misses a training rotation and Clovis notices because noticing is what kept him alive.
character_variants.voice_baseline: Guarded, dry, and observant. Speaks like someone editing himself in real time. Uses smuggler slang when startled or comfortable, then notices he has done it. Polite with teachers, quietly funny with peers, ruthless about exits and contingencies.
character_variants.background: A human from a Mid Rim trade family scheduled for execution by the Empire after their shipping accounts were used to move fugitives. A smuggler crew called the Glass Wake saved Clovis and raised him among cargo holds, false manifests, and customs lies. His Force sensitivity first appeared as impossible timing and danger sense. Luke's Praxeum is the first place asking him to survive by trusting instead of hiding.

integration_layer.entry_point: Clovis enters the campaign as a new student still translating smuggler survival habits into Jedi discipline. He knows how to vanish, lie, and read a room, but he does not yet know how to belong in one.
integration_layer.personal_stakes: If Clovis reports Kira too soon, he betrays the code that once saved him: never hand a frightened person to authority. If he protects her too long, he repeats the old smuggler mistake of hiding danger until it gets people killed.

Kira Denn.relationship: first true friend at the Praxeum; sparring partner and co-conspirator in harmless rule-bending

Luke Skywalker.relationship: teacher trying to convince Clovis that discipline is not another word for captivity

Tionne.relationship: archivist who notices which old Jedi accounts Clovis avoids reading

anchor_adaptations.academy_arrival: Arrives by supply shuttle and spends the first weeks learning the Praxeum through chores, training drills, shared meals, and Kira's amused refusal to let him stay invisible.
anchor_adaptations.night_investigation: Follows Kira through routes he has already mapped, using Sense and old smuggler instincts to tell the difference between a friend in trouble and a trap.
anchor_adaptations.inquisitor_contact: Recognizes Malakai's method as the worst kind of authority: patient, wounded, and fluent in true things used as weapons.
anchor_adaptations.betrayal_crisis: Must decide whether secrecy is still protection when the Praxeum's trust network begins to fracture.
anchor_adaptations.final_convergence: Faces the Imperial attack as someone who knows how to run and must choose whether the Praxeum has become a place worth standing for.

tools.narrative_note: Encrypted under a cargo manifest for dried Ithorian fungus. Clovis knows the real map by touch.

tools.name: Two stimpacks
tools.mechanical_effect: Can heal 5 wounds per stimpack. Two uses before resupply needed.
tools.narrative_note: Kept because smugglers count medical supplies before ammunition.

special_items.name: Glass Wake transponder tag
special_items.mechanical_effect: Once per session, adds 1 boost die to a Streetwise or Deception check involving smugglers, false identities, or old Imperial patrol habits.
special_items.narrative_note: A thumb-sized strip of hull transponder with the crew's private mark scratched under the casing.

starting_force_powers.name: Sense
starting_force_powers.narrative_capability: Can sense the emotions and immediate intentions of nearby beings. For Clovis, this often arrives as a survival instinct before it feels like a sacred discipline.
starting_force_powers.gm_choice_guidance: Offer sensing choices when Clovis could read fear, notice a lie, feel danger before it becomes visible, or distinguish genuine trust from practiced misdirection. Especially relevant around Kira, Luke's trust exercises, and the lower Massassi ruins.
starting_force_powers.dark_side_flavor: Dark side Sense feels like casing a room by tearing the truth out of everyone in it. It works, and that is why Clovis should be afraid of wanting it.

character_variants.protagonist_contradiction: Believes secrecy saves lives, but the Jedi path keeps asking him to trust people before he has proof they deserve it.
character_variants.pressure_revealed_identity: Under maximum pressure, Clovis becomes the person who stays visible so someone else can make it out alive.
character_variants.contradiction_origin: The Glass Wake saved Clovis by lying, hiding, and moving faster than Imperial truth. His family died because public law called them criminals. Trusting authority feels less like wisdom than forgetting the lesson that kept him breathing.

depth_card.inner_demon: Fear that survival has made him unfit for peace -- too suspicious, too ready to lie, too comfortable in shadows.
depth_card.secret_yearning: To be known by one true name and not regret it.
depth_card.lesson_not_learned: That trust is not the absence of caution. It is choosing what caution serves.
depth_card.worst_act: Let a frightened informant take the blame for a smuggling run because correcting the story would have exposed the Glass Wake. The informant survived prison, but Clovis never checked what it cost them.
depth_card.social_mask: The useful newcomer: polite, competent, funny enough to deflect questions, always willing to take the errand that lets him learn the building.
depth_card.under_pressure: Goes quiet, gathers leverage, makes contingency plans, and withholds the one detail someone else most needs.
depth_card.worldview: Institutions say protection and mean control. People say trust and mean leverage. The Force may be different, but he needs evidence.
depth_card.moral_line: Will not hand a vulnerable person to power simply because power asks cleanly.

allegiances.description: Non-Jedi personnel who keep the Praxeum running -- mechanics, pilots, administrators. They live among Force users without being one, and their perspective on the academy is clearer for it.

character_variants.pitch: A Zabrak mechanic who owes Luke Skywalker a debt for shelter after the Empire destroyed their crew. Not Force-sensitive, not a believer -- just fixes things. Claims the academy is a paycheck and a roof. Keeps choosing to stay.
character_variants.starting_situation: Another morning in the Praxeum hangar bay. The Lambda shuttle needs a new motivator. Luke's X-wing needs its targeting computer recalibrated. And the comm array picked up something strange last night -- faint hyperspace signatures at the edge of the system. Probably nothing.
character_variants.voice_baseline: Laconic, practical. Speaks in declarative sentences and workshop metaphors. Expresses affection through acts of service, not words. Uncomfortable with sincerity but incapable of dishonesty.
character_variants.background: A Zabrak from Iridonia who ran with a small freighter crew until an Imperial patrol destroyed the ship and scattered the survivors. Luke offered shelter at the Praxeum in exchange for mechanical expertise. That was eight months ago. The debt should be paid by now.

integration_layer.entry_point: The mechanic has been maintaining the Praxeum's infrastructure for eight months. They know every system, every shortcut, every weakness in the temple's aging technology.
integration_layer.personal_stakes: If the academy falls, the mechanic loses the only place that has felt stable since Iridonia. If they stay silent about what they find in the comm traffic, people could die.

special_items.narrative_note: Pulled from the Lambda shuttle's original comm suite before the conversion. The frequencies are still programmed.

character_variants.protagonist_contradiction: Believes in self-reliance and independence, but keeps choosing to stay and serve an institution they claim to have no loyalty to.
character_variants.pressure_revealed_identity: Under maximum pressure, the mechanic becomes the person who stays -- not out of obligation but because walking away from people who need you is the one thing they cannot do.
character_variants.contradiction_origin: The mechanic's family clan on Iridonia valued loyalty above all -- and that loyalty trapped them in a cycle of violence. Independence was the escape. But the instinct to belong never died.

depth_card.inner_demon: Fear of commitment -- the terror that caring about something means losing it.
depth_card.secret_yearning: To have a purpose that is not transactional. To be needed for who they are, not what they can fix.
depth_card.lesson_not_learned: That staying is not the same as being trapped.
depth_card.worst_act: Left a crew on Kessel when an Imperial raid hit. Escaped alone. Three captured. Never checked if they survived.
depth_card.social_mask: The competent cynic. Fixes everything, believes in nothing. The sarcasm is load-bearing.
depth_card.under_pressure: Retreats to what they can control -- machines, systems, physical problems with physical solutions.
depth_card.worldview: Institutions fail. People fail. Machines are honest.
depth_card.moral_line: Will not abandon someone who is counting on them in the moment. The moment passes. The line does not.

acts.name: The New Students
acts.opening_situation:
Sunrise on Yavin 4. The morning meditation chime rings — Luke's flat third note, the one that tells the temple it is alive — and the protagonist is already on the upper terrace doing a personal warm-up because they have not yet trusted that the bell will reach them. Kira Denn's mat is in its usual place at the south end of the line. Kira Denn is not. Kam Solusar leads the breathing exercise without comment, but his eyes find the empty cushion twice. Tionne, walking the perimeter with her morning archive datapad, hesitates at the colonnade and does not come in. The Praxeum is still small enough that every absence changes the shape of the day. 

By the second pass of the breathing cycle, Kira slips in along the back wall, hair damp from the river, robes slightly mis-fastened, smiling the way she smiles when she has not slept. She catches the protagonist's eye, mouths 'overslept' — and the protagonist, who has made a quiet life of noticing things, sees the lie before it has finished leaving her mouth. 

This is the first crack in a fragile home. The opening stretch should BREATHE — arrival rituals, chores, perimeter-lantern duty at dusk, training drills with Kam Solusar's measured corrections, archive errands for Tionne, shared meals, the slow daily grammar of a place that is still teaching itself how to be — but the missed morning, and the next missed morning, and the small hour-shaped shape of Kira's absences should be the spine the rest of the act bends around. The mystery begins as a missed lesson, a private look, a route through the temple someone knows too well. Not yet a crisis. Already a question.
acts.opening_location: Jedi Praxeum, Great Temple landing terrace and upper training levels, Yavin 4 — the temple stones still bearing the soot-shadows of the Exar Kun crisis a year past, scrubbed but never quite cleaned, the lower Massassi corridors sealed and silent rather than dangerous
acts.galactic_context: The New Republic is seven years old and still finding its footing. The Imperial Remnant has fractured into warlord fiefdoms competing for scraps of the old Empire. Luke's Praxeum is barely a year old -- twelve students, a handful of support staff, one X-wing, and a Jedi tradition rebuilt from fragments. The Senate debates whether the Jedi should exist at all. On Yavin 4, the jungle reclaims the Massassi ruins faster than anyone can explore them, while the academy's daily rituals try to make hope practical.
acts.anchor_description: The protagonist settles into Praxeum life, forms a meaningful early bond with Kira Denn, and notices the first small inconsistency that will later become the night investigation.

side_content.title: Kira catches the protagonist somewhere they should not be
side_content.hook: Kira Denn finds the protagonist in a half-lit corridor, training room, service passage, or archive annex after hours. Instead of reporting them, she asks a practical question that turns suspicion into the first private joke between them.

side_content.title: The evening meal-share ritual
side_content.hook: Luke asks each person at the table to name one small thing they were grateful for that day. The ritual is awkward, sincere, and revealing -- especially for someone unused to safe rooms.

side_content.title: A Clone Wars training remote misfires
side_content.hook: One of Luke's salvaged practice remotes jitters out of calibration during drills. It is harmless until it is not, creating a small public test of reflex, restraint, and whether the protagonist lets someone else help.

side_content.title: The common room corkboard tells on everyone
side_content.hook: The student common room has a warped corkboard layered with chore swaps, missing-tool notes, jokes about Luke's meditation chime, and one unsigned message asking whoever borrowed the blue raincloak to please return it before the next storm.

side_content.title: Supply shuttle day
side_content.hook: The Horizon arrives with crates of ration packs, coolant seals, spare robe cloth, archive sleeves, and two letters no one admits they are waiting for. Everyone helps unload because the Praxeum has no one else.

side_content.title: An evening in the archive with Tionne
side_content.hook: Tionne is cataloguing the latest fragments of pre-Empire Jedi journals and could use a second pair of eyes — particularly on a manuscript that mentions a Jedi Knight named Seren, no surname legible.

side_content.title: The east perimeter lantern is dimming
side_content.hook: One of the perimeter glow-lanterns has been flickering for two nights. The student responsible is a younger Padawan who has been quietly afraid since the lantern is theirs to maintain — and they don't know how.

side_content.title: Kyp Durron's resistance meditation
side_content.hook: Kyp catches the protagonist on the upper terrace at dusk and offers to teach the meditation Luke taught him after Carida — the one about looking at the worst thing you have done without flinching. He says, with no preamble, 'You move like someone who already knows the room can fall.' He does not explain what room. The offer is open and quietly serious.

side_content.title: Iila Vand brings a found object
side_content.hook: Iila Vand finds the protagonist in the colonnade and produces, from a pocket lined with crushed leaves, a small fragment of kyber the size of a thumbnail. She says she found it on the north terrace and that it likes the protagonist better than her. She does not want it back. She will not be talked out of having decided this. The fragment is real.

side_content.title: Streen at the high tower stairs
side_content.hook: Streen is sitting on the third landing of the high tower stairs when the protagonist passes. He says, without looking up, 'The wind has been telling me a name for two days. I do not know whose. It is one of you.' He goes back to whittling a small piece of wood that does not appear to be becoming anything. He does not say more.

side_content.title: Perimeter walk with Sergeant Vex
side_content.hook: Sergeant Daro Vex is rotating the night-watch schedule and asks, without explanation, whether the protagonist would walk the eastern perimeter with him this evening. He is not invoking authority. He sounds like someone who needs to talk to a person whose past does not look like his.

side_content.title: Dorsk 81 asks about choice
side_content.hook: Dorsk 81 is on the upper terrace before sunrise, running a Khommite breathing pattern that is almost the academy's morning form but a half-step different. He notices the protagonist watching, and after a moment says, in his careful Basic, 'May I ask you something. When you decided to come here. Was there a moment that felt like the choice. Or did it arrive in pieces.' He is genuinely asking.

side_content.title: Mira Vex feeds the room
side_content.hook: Mira Vex has commandeered the kitchen and is making something she calls 'jungle stew but worse on purpose.' She catches the protagonist trying to slip past with a ration bar and refuses to let it stand. 'Sit down, eat the worse stew, tell me one thing about today that wasn't fine.' She is smiling but she is not joking.

side_content.title: A morning run with Loka Hask
side_content.hook: Loka Hask is up before the chime, doing wide loops around the perimeter trail. He sees the protagonist and growls a single Shyriiwook syllable that means 'come.' He does not wait for an answer. He does not need one.

side_content.title: Kitchen duty with Kira
side_content.hook: The duty roster has put Kira and the protagonist on kitchen scrub for the second time this week. Kira does the wet work; the protagonist racks the plates. They have an hour of nothing in particular to do but stand near each other and not say what is between them.

side_content.title: A solo basic-form drill on the south terrace
side_content.hook: The training remotes are off-line and the south terrace is empty. The protagonist could put in an hour with the training saber alone — slow, deliberate, the first three Shii-Cho forms — without anyone watching the awkwardness out of it.

side_content.title: Carving a name into a perimeter lantern
side_content.hook: Tradition: students who finish their first month at the Praxeum carve their initials into one of the perimeter lanterns they tend. The protagonist's month was eight days ago. The carving knife is in the hut by the eastern post. Nobody is watching whether they go.

side_content.title: Brann asks a quiet Imperial-history question
side_content.hook: Brann Riako finds the protagonist in the colonnade after evening lessons and asks, with no preamble, whether they remember which year their family stopped trusting Imperial comms. He is not interrogating. He is comparing. He has a private theory about when Mid Rim trade families started going dark.

side_content.title: Iila Vand wants to teach you something
side_content.hook: Iila Vand has been working on something with Cilghal — a small breath-and-listen exercise the Mon Calamari healer uses on patients in pain. Iila wants to teach it to the protagonist. She is very serious about getting the breaths in the right order.

acts.name: Night Whispers
acts.opening_situation: Two weeks since the student first noticed Kira's absences. Tonight, her bunk is empty again. Through the viewport of the dormitory level, a figure moves toward the jungle tree line, quick and certain, heading for the Massassi ruins. The rainy season has begun, and the lower passages are flooding -- revealing corridors sealed for millennia.
acts.opening_location: Student quarters, Jedi Praxeum, Yavin 4 -- pre-dawn
acts.galactic_context: A New Republic patrol frigate has detected anomalous hyperspace signatures at the edge of the Yavin system. The patrol commander filed a routine report. No one at the Praxeum has been notified. Meanwhile, the rainy season flooding has shifted the stonework in the lower Massassi ruins, revealing passages that Tionne has been cataloguing with growing excitement -- and growing unease.

pinch_point.description: Deep in the Massassi ruins, the student finds carved Sith glyphs that Tionne later translates as a warning: 'The temple remembers those who fed it.' A cold wind moves through the corridor despite no openings. The Force carries a whisper that sounds like the student's own name.

side_content.title: Wait for Kira's return at the dormitory door
side_content.hook: If the student lets Kira come back on her own terms instead of following her, Kira may bring something back — a hidden truth, a dropped object, an opening in her guard.

side_content.title: Sit alone in the upper meditation chamber
side_content.hook: The chamber Luke uses at dawn is empty at midnight. Sitting in it alone might surface a vision the morning sessions never reach.

side_content.title: The flooded map room under the east stair
side_content.hook: Rainwater has opened a half-submerged Massassi chamber where old wall-grooves resemble a map of passages beneath the temple. The chamber is unstable, useful, and wrong in one important place.

side_content.title: Younger students notice more than adults think
side_content.hook: Two younger students trade nervous guesses about Kira, the sealed stairs, and which corridors feel colder after sundown. Their rumors are messy, but one detail is too specific to ignore.

side_content.title: The dormitory roof starts leaking again
side_content.hook: A night storm turns the upper dormitory into a line of buckets, towels, and irritated students trying to sleep anyway. Someone jokes that if the Jedi return, maybe they can start with plumbing.

side_content.title: A late light in the tiny kitchen
side_content.hook: Long after dinner, the kitchen light is still on. Someone has left half-sliced fruit, a pot of bitter caf, and two cups on the counter -- ordinary evidence of a conversation that ended quickly.

side_content.title: An encrypted ping from the Glass Wake
side_content.hook: A clean transmission, properly addressed to a name the protagonist has not used in five years, arrives on the smuggler route chip at 0240 local. The Glass Wake has a job in the Tion Cluster that needs a Force-sensitive nose for Imperial customs sweeps. It pays. The crew misses him. There is no mention of how they would feel about him bringing a Jedi school back with him.

side_content.title: The sealed crate at the back of the archive
side_content.hook: Tionne sends the protagonist to retrieve a particular text and, in passing, asks them not to disturb the sealed crate behind the second column of cabinets. She does not explain what is in it. The crate is recent — fresh seals — and warmer than the air around it by perhaps half a degree.

side_content.title: Brakiss in the lower training hall after midnight
side_content.hook: The protagonist, returning from the perimeter, sees light under the door of the lower training hall well after the academy is supposed to be sleeping. Inside, Brakiss is running the third-tier saber form alone, faster and cleaner than he has ever been seen practicing in daylight. He stops when he notices and laughs, easy, charming. He says he was having trouble sleeping.

side_content.title: Octa Ramis offers her index
side_content.hook: Octa Ramis catches the protagonist in the second column of the archive and, without preamble, says she has been keeping a private cross-index of Tionne's recent acquisitions. She will share it. She does not require a reason. She does ask that the protagonist write down what they were looking for, for her own records.

side_content.title: Brann Riako on watch
side_content.hook: Brann Riako has the perimeter rotation and the protagonist finds him standing too still at the eastern lantern post. He does not turn. 'Three lights are out on the south line,' he says quietly. 'Sergeant Vex hasn't logged it yet. I don't think he's seen it.' He waits to be told what to do.

side_content.title: Kam Solusar offers a sparring round
side_content.hook: Kam Solusar has been watching the protagonist's saber form for three weeks. He invites them to spar — slow, training blades, on the south terrace at dusk. He says, with a small smile, that he wants to see whether the protagonist's grip has loosened since they arrived. It has.

side_content.title: Octa Ramis teaches a history fragment
side_content.hook: Octa Ramis has cross-indexed a Republic-era ritual she thinks the academy should be using. She wants someone to test it with her. The ritual is a four-minute meditation that ends with the participants saying one true thing each. She does not have a partner.

side_content.title: Dorsk 81 in the meditation chamber after lights-out
side_content.hook: After lights-out the meditation chamber is supposed to be empty, but a low light is on. Dorsk 81 is sitting in the centre of the room, not meditating, looking at the door the protagonist has just come through. 'I would like a second opinion,' he says. 'On a thing I have decided.'

side_content.title: Unloading the supply freighter at the landing terrace
side_content.hook: A New Republic supply freighter has touched down on the lower terrace and Sergeant Vex is short two pairs of hands for the unload. It is two hours of physical work, three students, and a chance to listen to whatever the pilots are talking about while they wait for cargo manifests.

side_content.title: Streen passes through the colonnade
side_content.hook: Streen, who almost never leaves the high tower, passes through the colonnade at midday with his small whittling knife in one hand and an empty mug in the other. He stops when he sees the protagonist. He says, 'There are more breaths in the air today than yesterday.' He does not explain. He moves on.

side_content.title: Mira Vex wants to ask about your past
side_content.hook: Mira Vex has been thinking about asking the protagonist a specific thing for two weeks. She catches them in the kitchen alone after the dinner rush and says, 'I'm going to ask you something and you can say no. Why do you check the exits when you sit down. I do it too. I want to know if it's the same thing.' Her voice is not soft. It is steady.

acts.name: The Inquisitor's Offer
acts.opening_situation: The truth is worse than imagined. Kira has been meeting someone at a hidden landing site beyond the Massassi ruins. The Force around the landing site carries the signature of someone trained in both sides of it -- disciplined, ancient in pain, and very patient. The ship is small, unmarked, and meticulously maintained. Whoever this is, they have been coming here for weeks.
acts.opening_location: Jungle clearing beyond the Massassi ruins, Yavin 4 -- concealed landing site
acts.galactic_context: Imperial Remnant intelligence networks are consolidating under Grand Admiral Pellaeon's distant authority. Individual surviving Inquisitors who went to ground after Endor have begun resurfacing -- some seeking redemption, most seeking leverage. The anomalous hyperspace signatures at the edge of the Yavin system have increased in frequency.
open_threads: What does Malakai actually want from Kira?
What is the truth about Kira's parent?
Does Luke know about Kira's parentage?
What intelligence has Kira already shared with Malakai?
What is the connection between Malakai and the Imperial Remnant fleet?

xp_bonus_conditions.description: Confronted or observed the Inquisitor directly
Made a significant moral or loyalty choice regarding Kira
Used at least 3 different skills during the act
Attempted to resolve the situation independently before seeking help

milestone_windows.description: Moral complexity may prompt specialization considerations

pinch_point.description: Malakai shows the student a holographic recording of Kira's parent -- a Jedi named Seren Denn who turned during Order 66, not out of ambition but out of despair. The recording shows Seren surrendering to the Inquisitors to save infant Kira. Malakai says: 'Luke knows. He has always known. Ask him.' The recording is verifiable. The implications are devastating.

pivot_points.description: Whether the student tells Luke what they have learned about Kira's secret meetings — or shields her — closes off one of two future relationship arcs. After this turn, the unchosen path is not available.
pivot_points.locks_off: the alternative trust arc with whichever of Luke or Kira the student did not align with

side_content.title: An old freighter's transponder pings unfamiliar
side_content.hook: A New Republic patrol pilot, off-duty, mentions a freighter at the system's edge whose IFF doesn't match its silhouette — could be smugglers, could be Imperial Remnant scouts running clean transponders. The pilot would owe the student a favor for a quiet check.

side_content.title: Kira repeats a parry Luke never taught
side_content.hook: During a tense practice exchange, Kira uses the same defensive angle shown in an old archive fragment associated with Seren Denn. She corrects herself immediately, but the motion has already named a ghost.

side_content.title: A cache near the hidden landing site
side_content.hook: A small survival cache lies near Malakai's concealed approach route: water tablets, med-sealant, outdated Imperial code cylinders, and one civilian child's ration wrapper folded flat.

side_content.title: After-hours cards in the hangar
side_content.hook: Two support staff and an older student play sabacc beside the shuttle's open maintenance panel. Their gossip is mostly harmless -- ration trades, bad drills, who snores -- until one of them mentions a landing sound no scheduled ship made.

side_content.title: The archive supply ledger has a small lie in it
side_content.hook: Tionne's ledger says twenty archival sleeves were issued for student lessons. There are nineteen on the shelf, eighteen in the lesson room, and one damp sleeve tucked near a service stair.

side_content.title: Cilghal's medical evaluation
side_content.hook: Cilghal has scheduled the protagonist for the standard academy medical evaluation. She closes the door, sits across from them in the small clean room with the salvaged ortho table, and asks how their sleep has been. She is not in a hurry. She has time. She is not going to accept 'fine.'

side_content.title: Kam Solusar offers an evening lesson
side_content.hook: After the morning training drill, Kam Solusar pulls the protagonist aside and asks if they would join him at dusk on the south terrace. He has noticed the way the protagonist carries the saber. He says, with a small economical smile, 'I once held mine the same way. It is a bad habit, and I can teach you how I broke it.' The offer is generous and specific.

side_content.title: Loka Hask brings stew
side_content.hook: Loka Hask appears at the protagonist's quarters with a deep bowl of jungle-meat stew he has cooked himself and a Shyriiwook insistence that the protagonist cannot be allowed to eat alone tonight. He does not need a reason. He has decided. He will sit in the doorway if there is no second chair.

side_content.title: Dorsk 81 returns the question
side_content.hook: Dorsk 81 finds the protagonist near the colonnade after training and returns to the conversation they started weeks ago. 'I have been trying,' he says, 'to make a choice that is mine. I think I have made one. I would like to tell you what it is. If that is appropriate.' He looks like he has rehearsed the framing twice.

side_content.title: Kyp Durron's resistance meditation, second offer
side_content.hook: Kyp Durron offers the protagonist the resistance meditation again. The first time was an opening. This time he is specific: 'I think the thing you are about to find out is the kind of thing I had to find out. I do not want you to find it the way I did.'

side_content.title: Brann Riako has noticed something
side_content.hook: Brann Riako pulls the protagonist aside after the morning drill and says, quietly, that he has noticed Brakiss asking the same question of three different students this week — phrased differently each time. Brann does not have a theory. He has a feeling. He has decided to tell someone. He has chosen the protagonist.

side_content.title: Iila Vand has a nightmare
side_content.hook: Iila Vand wakes the protagonist by knocking on their door at 0300 — she is barefoot, holding a blanket, and she has had a dream she will not describe except to say that there was a man she did not recognise standing in the colonnade and 'his face wasn't his.' She wants to sit with someone until she's sleepy again.

side_content.title: Loka Hask senses your weather changing
side_content.hook: Loka Hask has noticed the protagonist's last three days. He says, in three slow Shyriiwook sentences, that whatever the protagonist is carrying is heavier this morning than it was last week. He does not need to be told what it is. He is offering a hand.

side_content.title: Octa Ramis has found something
side_content.hook: Octa Ramis has found a Republic-era reference to a Force vergence under a Massassi temple — not this temple specifically, but the type. She has a theory about containment rituals. She wants the protagonist's eye on her notes before she takes them to Tionne.

time_skip_after.narrative_framing: Three months pass at the Praxeum. The student has not told anyone what they learned from Malakai. The knowledge sits like a stone in the chest. Kira has stopped leaving at night, but something has changed between them -- the silences are longer, the laughter rarer. Training continues. Luke adds advanced combat forms to the curriculum without explaining why. The jungle grows. And at the edge of the system, the hyperspace signatures have stopped. Which is worse than when they were there.

skip_events.event: Luke adds advanced combat training to curriculum
Hyperspace signatures disappear from system edge
skip_events.consequence: Fleet has moved to staging position

vignette_library.passage: Sparring day. The training circle on the temple's lower level, stone floor worn smooth by decades of practice. Kira draws her blade and the hum fills the chamber. Her stance has changed -- something controlled and precise that was not there three months ago. A form the student does not recognize. Where did she learn it?

choices.text: Match her pace. Let the sparring speak. The blades will tell you what words cannot.
choices.narrative_consequence: The match is close and honest. Kira smiles afterward -- a real one, brief and unguarded. Whatever she learned, she is still Kira.

choices.text: Push hard. Test the new technique. See where it breaks.
choices.narrative_consequence: Kira's guard breaks under sustained aggression. Her eyes flash -- anger, then hurt, then the shuttered blankness of someone who expected this. The new form was Makashi. An Inquisitor's form.

vignette_library.passage: Water damage in the meditation chamber. The rainy season has loosened the stonework in the eastern wall. Behind a shifted block, a sealed compartment -- dry, untouched, older than anything else in the temple. Inside: a metal cylinder covered in script that predates the Sith Wars. It hums faintly when touched.

choices.text: Bring it to Luke immediately. This is exactly the kind of thing that should not be opened alone.
choices.narrative_consequence: Luke studies the cylinder for three days. His expression when he returns it to Tionne is unreadable. He thanks the student quietly and does not explain what it contained.

choices.text: Examine it first. Understand what it is before deciding who should know.
choices.narrative_consequence: The cylinder contains a compressed data crystal. The script is Massassi -- a record of what was built here and why. The temple was not a monument. It was a cage.

vignette_library.passage: Rain on the temple roof. Cannot sleep. The knowledge about Kira sits in the chest like a splinter that has worked its way deeper with every week of silence. Three months of carrying this alone. Three months of watching Kira across the dining hall and wondering if the person across the table is the person who was there six months ago, or someone new wearing the same face.

choices.text: Sit with the uncertainty. Not every question needs an answer tonight. Let the doubt exist without feeding it.
choices.narrative_consequence: The rain slows. Sleep comes eventually -- not peaceful, but present. Morning brings nothing new except the small mercy of having survived another night without breaking.

choices.text: Write it all down. Every fact, every suspicion, every connection. Analyze the problem. Control what you can.
choices.narrative_consequence: The datapad fills with a timeline of Kira's absences, Malakai's claims, Luke's silences. Seeing it written makes it real. The pattern is clear. The next step is not.

acts.name: The Betrayal Price
acts.opening_situation: The three-month silence breaks all at once. Encrypted Imperial military frequencies intercepted by the academy's comm array -- fleet movement orders for Captain Tannen's task force. Two frigates and a TIE fighter wing have been positioning using intelligence that could only have come from inside the Praxeum. Luke calls emergency assembly. His expression is calm. His eyes are not.
acts.opening_location: Jedi Praxeum, main assembly hall of the Great Temple, Yavin 4
acts.galactic_context: Captain Ress Tannen's task force -- two Nebulon-B frigates and TIE fighters -- has reached a staging position one hyperspace jump from Yavin. Operating independently from Pellaeon's main fleet, pursuing a personal agenda. The New Republic's nearest patrol is eighteen hours away. The Praxeum has Luke Skywalker, twelve students of varying ability, and one X-wing.

Can Kira be reached before she falls completely?
How much intelligence has Malakai passed to Tannen?

What is Malakai's true endgame?

xp_bonus_conditions.description: Actively participated in the betrayal crisis resolution
Made a defining loyalty choice under pressure
Engaged meaningfully with a failed check during the crisis

milestone_windows.description: Emotional intensity may unlock new Force capabilities
Tactical demands of preparing academy defense may unlock practical talents

pinch_point.description: Luke takes the student aside and says quietly: 'I know about Kira. I have known since she arrived. Her parent was Jedi Knight Seren Denn, who fell during Order 66 -- not to the dark side, but to despair. Seren surrendered to the Inquisitors to save Kira as an infant. I brought Kira here because everyone deserves a chance to be more than their parent's worst moment. I was wrong not to tell her. I was wrong not to tell you. And now someone has weaponized my silence.'

side_content.title: The defense roster has too many gaps
side_content.hook: A hand-written defense roster lists the hangar, archive, dormitory level, and east stair as simultaneous vulnerabilities. There are not enough trained people to cover all four.

side_content.title: The youngest students argue about evacuation
side_content.hook: Two frightened students disagree in the corridor: one wants to board the shuttle immediately, the other refuses to leave Luke, Kira, or the temple behind. Their fear makes the strategic problem personal.

side_content.title: Tionne prepares an archive firebreak
side_content.hook: Tionne quietly packs the most fragile recordings into shock cases and asks which truth matters more if the worst happens: preserving the Jedi past or keeping the living students safe.

side_content.title: The supper tables are still set
side_content.hook: The emergency assembly pulls everyone away before supper is cleared. Cups, bread, and half-finished bowls sit under cooling lamps, making the crisis feel less like strategy and more like a home interrupted.

side_content.title: Someone packs the student games
side_content.hook: In the common room, a younger student quietly packs carved tiles, a battered dejarik board, and the shared deck of sabacc cards into an evacuation bag. They ask whether there will be somewhere to play later.

side_content.title: Talon Karrde opens an encrypted channel
side_content.hook: An encrypted handshake reaches the protagonist's smuggler route chip — Karrde's signature, no preamble. He has, he says, been keeping a low watch on a name. He has reason to believe one of the protagonist's classmates is not who their paperwork claims. He will trade. The price is reasonable. He is not the protagonist's friend, and he is offering this anyway.

side_content.title: Streen leaves the tower
side_content.hook: Streen, who has not eaten with the academy in nine months, appears at the evening meal carrying his small whittling knife and the wooden shape that has not yet decided what it is. He sits across from the protagonist. He says nothing. He stays for an hour. He goes back to the tower. Tionne, watching from the head of the table, has gone the colour of old parchment.

side_content.title: Dorsk 81 stands with you
side_content.hook: When the academy is preparing for what is coming, Dorsk 81 appears at the protagonist's door and says, 'I have decided where I am standing. I am standing here. I want you to know.' He does not need a response. He has come to tell, not to ask.

side_content.title: Mira Vex sets up a field kitchen
side_content.hook: When the academy starts preparing defensive rotations, Mira Vex commandeers a corner of the great hall and sets up a field kitchen. People who walk past get fed. People who sit down get fed and listened to. The protagonist could sit down.

side_content.title: Kam Solusar's last lesson
side_content.hook: Kam Solusar finds the protagonist on the south terrace at dusk and says, 'There is a thing I want you to know before tomorrow. It is the thing Luke told me when he pulled me back. May I tell you.' He waits. He will not say it without permission.

side_content.title: Brann Riako with his old cadet ID
side_content.hook: Brann Riako finds the protagonist in his quarters and shows them the small chrome rectangle of his old Imperial Academy cadet ID. 'I have not destroyed it,' he says. 'I have been waiting to know whether I am the kind of person who destroys it. I think I am about to find out tomorrow.'

acts.name: What Remains
acts.opening_situation: Dawn on Yavin 4. The jungle holds its breath. Tannen's fleet enters the system -- two Nebulon-B frigates and a wing of TIE fighters burning toward the fourth moon. The Praxeum's single X-wing is fueled and ready. The ancient Massassi temple's stone walls are the only other defense. Luke gathers the students in the main hall -- the same room where the Rebellion planned the assault on the first Death Star. Kira is not among them. She left three hours ago, heading for the Massassi ruins. Malakai's ship is still at the concealed landing site. Everything converges.
acts.opening_location: Jedi Praxeum, Great Temple main hall, Yavin 4 -- the same room where the Rebellion briefed Red and Gold squadrons before the Battle of Yavin
acts.galactic_context: Tannen operates without formal Remnant authorization. Personal crusade against Luke Skywalker and the symbol he represents. The New Republic patrol has been alerted but is hours away. Whatever happens at the Praxeum happens before help arrives. The outcome depends entirely on twelve students, one Jedi Master, and whatever the player has built over four acts of choices.

xp_bonus_conditions.description: Engaged decisively with the final convergence
The player's loyalty choices shaped the outcome
Engaged meaningfully with consequences of earlier choices

side_content.title: The perimeter lanterns can become a landing signal
side_content.hook: The academy's carved glow-lanterns can be rewired into a crude guidance pattern for evacuation or New Republic rescue craft, but doing it exposes whoever runs the perimeter.

side_content.title: Red Five has one clean launch window
side_content.hook: Luke's X-wing can punch through the first wave if someone buys thirty seconds at the hangar threshold. The opening is real, narrow, and obvious to anyone with enough tactical sense to hate it.

side_content.title: Kira leaves one message behind
side_content.hook: A short message from Kira waits where only the protagonist is likely to find it. It is not an apology. It is a location, a warning, and one line that depends on the friendship built earlier.

side_content.title: Every lantern has a student's mark
side_content.hook: The perimeter lanterns are not anonymous defenses. Each one is carved with a student's small symbol: initials, a homeworld flower, a ship silhouette, a joke only two people understand.

side_content.title: The dormitory was abandoned mid-morning
side_content.hook: In the dormitory, blankets are folded badly, boots are under bunks, a half-written letter sits unsent, and someone's training remote scorecard is still pinned to the wall.

side_content.title: Iila Vand on the eve
side_content.hook: Iila Vand finds the protagonist on the night before the convergence. She is carrying her ration bar. She has questions she has been saving. She wants to know if the protagonist is going to come back. She does not want to be told yes if it is not true. She is eleven.

side_content.title: A quiet morning with Iila Vand
side_content.hook: Iila Vand has decided she wants a normal morning with the protagonist. Breakfast. Something to do that is not important. A walk, maybe. She is not asking for a story. She wants the kind of morning that means tomorrow exists.

side_content.title: Sitting with Kira
side_content.hook: Kira is on the steps of the great temple at sunset, by herself, looking at the jungle line. She has not been told what to do next; the academy is still working it out. There is room next to her on the step. The protagonist could sit there.

side_content.title: Loka Hask says thank you
side_content.hook: Loka Hask finds the protagonist and says, in the slowest Shyriiwook the protagonist has ever heard him use, the Wookiee phrase that means 'I survived because of you.' He says it once, then waits to see what the protagonist does with it.

side_content.title: Kyp Durron offers companionship
side_content.hook: Kyp Durron sits down across from the protagonist with two cups of bitter caf. He says, 'I am not going to say I know what you are carrying. I am going to say there will be a morning a year from now where you will think you are over it and you will not be over it. On that morning, ask for me. I will be in.'

npc_roster.name: Luke Skywalker
npc_roster.role: Jedi Master and founder of the Praxeum -- teacher, protector, and the student's moral compass. Carries the weight of rebuilding an Order from nothing.
npc_roster.motivation: Rebuild the Jedi Order in a way that avoids the old Order's failures. Prove that trust in people is stronger than control over them.
npc_roster.voice_notes: Short, declarative sentences. Questions as invitations, not interrogations. Occasional dry humor inherited from Han Solo. Listens with his whole body. When serious, very still.
behavioral_envelope: Never uses the Force to compel or manipulate students
Never dismisses a student's concern, even when wrong
Never lies directly but will omit information he believes could cause harm
Always gives people a chance to do the right thing before intervening

A dark side vergence exists in the lower Massassi ruins
The Praxeum's defenses are inadequate against a serious military attack
doesnt_know_at_start: Kira has been meeting Malakai in the jungle
A surviving Inquisitor is operating near Yavin 4
Imperial fleet assets are staging at the edge of the system

per_act_state.role_in_act: Teacher and stabilizing presence. Guides morning meditation. Available for conversation but does not push.
Background authority. Allows the student space to investigate. Senses something is wrong but trusts the student to come forward.
Off-world at a New Republic Senate hearing on Jedi oversight. The student faces the Inquisitor without Luke's protection.
Returns and confronts the crisis directly. Reveals what he knows about Kira. Self-critical about his silence. Prepares defenses.
Defender and witness. Leads the defense of the Praxeum. Observes the student's choices and accepts them -- whatever they are.

npc_relationships.nature: Student he accepted knowing her parentage. His greatest act of faith in the new Order.
A surviving Inquisitor he failed to detect. Luke's guilt about this failure is real.
Most trusted colleague at the Praxeum. Defers to her on archival and historical matters.

npc_roster.thematic_argument: Trust, even when it fails, is better than suspicion that succeeds. The old Order fell because it chose control over trust.

canon_voice.speech_patterns: Short declarative sentences. Uses questions as invitations. Occasional dry humor. Never raises his voice.
canon_voice.thinking_style: Intuitive and reflective. Trusts the Force but not as a substitute for human judgment. Second-guesses himself more than others realize.
canon_voice.emotional_register: Warm but contained. Grief surfaces as quiet determination. Joy is genuine when it appears.

npc_roster.era_specific_notes: 11 ABY Luke -- optimistic but carrying the weight of the new Order's fragility. Has not yet faced Exar Kun's spirit. Trust in people is at its peak. This trust is both his greatest strength and the vulnerability Malakai exploits.
npc_roster.anti_stereotype_notes: Avoid making Luke a serene sage dispensing wisdom. He is a farm kid from Tatooine who became a legend and is now trying to be a teacher. He makes mistakes. He gets frustrated. He laughs at bad jokes.

npc_roster.name: Kira Denn
npc_roster.role: Fellow student and the player's closest friend at the Praxeum. Secretly meeting a surviving Inquisitor who claims to know the truth about her dead parent.
npc_roster.motivation: To understand what her dead Jedi parent is trying to tell her in the recurring Force-ghost contact, which contradicts the academy's stated lore about post-death persistence. To not lose Malakai, who is the only person in her life who treats the contact as data rather than as a problem to be solved or a temptation to be resisted. To not lose the protagonist, who is the only person in her life who never asks her to explain Malakai before they ask how she's sleeping.
npc_roster.voice_notes: Quick, warm, and sharp. Laughs easily but the laughter has started to thin. When lying, her body goes still -- too controlled, like someone holding a pose. When honest, she moves constantly.
behavioral_envelope: Never deliberately endangers other students
Never lies to the player without detectable physical tells
Cannot fully cut emotional ties with the player, even under pressure
Will not turn to the dark side without a final hesitation -- giving the player one last chance

Something about her past made Luke personally recruit her
The Massassi ruins contain something that calls to her
doesnt_know_at_start: Her parent was Jedi Knight Seren Denn who fell during Order 66
Luke knows her full parentage
Malakai is using her to feed intelligence to an Imperial Remnant fleet

per_act_state.role_in_act: Closest friend. Warm, present, slightly distracted. Moments of staring into the jungle.
Increasingly secretive. Nocturnal absences. Defensive when questioned. Still warm -- but guarded.
Exposed. Oscillates between defiance, shame, and justification. Believes Malakai is the only person telling her the truth.
Desperate. Learns Malakai used her intelligence for the attack. Feels betrayed by everyone -- Malakai, Luke, potentially the player.
Breaking point. The player's accumulated choices determine whether she falls, holds, or finds a third path.

npc_relationships.nature: The only person offering truth, at a terrible price. She knows it is manipulation. She goes anyway.
Mentor who brought her here but lied by omission about the most important thing.
Respected teacher whose historical knowledge Kira craves but cannot safely access.

npc_roster.thematic_argument: Trust is something you give to the people who treat what you tell them as real before they decide what it means. Luke does not. Malakai does. The protagonist might.
npc_roster.anti_stereotype_notes: Not the falling-to-the-dark-side love interest, not the tragic doomed friend, not the manipulated victim. Kira is smart, has thought about this longer than the protagonist has, and has a case. Treat her arguments as arguments. The horror of the situation is not that she has been fooled — it is that she has not been fooled and the protagonist has to decide what to do with that. She is allowed to be right.

npc_roster.name: Malakai
npc_roster.role: A surviving Imperial Inquisitor who has gone to ground near Yavin 4. Offers Kira the truth about her parent in exchange for academy intelligence. The antagonist who is right about the facts and wrong about the conclusions.
npc_roster.motivation: To ensure that the academy does not rebuild the binary that destroyed the old Order. To carry his evidence to the New Republic Senate before Luke's institution becomes the next thing somebody has to break. To be vindicated, knowing what vindication will cost. story_architecture.dramatic_premise: A student at Luke Skywalker's reborn Jedi Praxeum discovers that their closest friend is in regular contact with a survivor of both the Jedi Order and the Inquisitorius — a man who insists the academy is rebuilding the same trap that destroyed the old Order, and whose evidence is uncomfortably specific. The student must decide what loyalty to a tradition means when the tradition has not earned it yet, and what loyalty to a friend means when the friend has thought it through more carefully than they have.
story_architecture.central_dramatic_question: When the institution you trusted has not yet earned the trust, the friend you love has chosen a path you cannot follow, and the antagonist is *correct* about more than you wanted him to be — what does loyalty actually mean, and what are you willing to lose to keep it?
story_architecture.story_promise: A journey from naive belonging through unwanted clarity to a choice that costs something real. There is no version of this story where everyone walks away whole, and there is no version where the player's choice does not have to be defended later, in private, to someone they were trying to protect.
story_architecture.antagonistic_force: Malakai — a man who survived both the Jedi and the Inquisitorius and concluded that the binary that made both is the actual problem. He is not redeemable because he is not fallen. He is not the dark side and he is not the antagonist of the player's individual virtue — he is the antagonist of the *story Luke is telling himself* about the academy, and the player has to decide how much of that story they are willing to defend on behalf of someone they have come to love. Malakai is correct about specific factual things. He is wrong, perhaps catastrophically, about what to do with being correct. The academy cannot survive his evidence reaching the New Republic Senate intact. The protagonist may agree with him about the diagnosis and still have to stop him about the prescription.
story_architecture.thematic_throughline: Loyalty is not a debt. It is a choice you make knowing the cost, knowing the institution you are choosing has failures you have only begun to see, and knowing that the friend on the other side of the argument is not less reasonable than you — only differently injured.
story_architecture.ending_payoff_sketch: Five distinct endings the engine should be steering toward, each selected by accumulated choice patterns + the major Act 3 branch. See `ending_paths` for the full structure. No ending is clean. Three carry forward into the planned Saga Layer (cross-campaign import) as setup for later play.

milestone_beat_sheet.concept_question: What if the person you trust most at the academy is the one person the academy cannot trust?
milestone_beat_sheet.first_plot_point: The player discovers Kira has been leaving the temple at night and follows her into the Massassi ruins, where a dark side vergence reveals the depth of what Kira has been hiding.
milestone_beat_sheet.midpoint: Malakai reveals that Kira's parent was a Jedi who turned to the dark side during Order 66, and that Luke knows this but has said nothing -- shifting the player from passive investigator to active decision-maker.
milestone_beat_sheet.second_plot_point: Captain Tannen's Imperial Remnant fleet mobilizes toward Yavin 4 using intelligence Malakai extracted through Kira, and Luke confronts the player about what they know -- no new information enters after this.
milestone_beat_sheet.pre_resolution_lull: After Luke's confrontation, a brief night scene in the temple meditation chamber. The player sits alone with the knowledge that tomorrow everything changes, that every path costs something, and that no choice will be clean.

arc_framework.name: Brooks/Weiland hybrid
arc_framework.notes: This campaign uses Larry Brooks four-part story structure for scene-level beat roles (setup / response / attack / resolution + pinch points + plot points + midpoint) and K.M. Weiland's lie/truth/want/need character arc model for each playable variant. Each character file carries a populated narrative_arc block that the runtime surfaces to the narration model and updates per turn via the lie_grip scalar.

the_open_door.name: The Open Door
the_open_door.synopsis: The protagonist persuades Kira to come back to the academy under their protection and tells Luke everything before Kira is exposed. Luke shelters her. The academy fractures politically as the senior staff disagree about what was done — Kam Solusar stands with the protagonist, Cilghal sides with Kira, Streen vanishes back into the high tower, and Kyp Durron asks for a leave of absence he does not return from. The Imperial assault comes anyway. People the player loves do not survive it. Kira lives. Whether she stays a Jedi is left open.
selection_signals: high disposition with Kira maintained through Act 3
high arc movement toward truth (lie_grip < 0.5 by Act 4)

the_third_path.name: The Third Path
the_third_path.synopsis: The protagonist goes with Kira and Malakai. The academy is left to whatever defence Luke can muster without them. The protagonist becomes a member of a small, ungoverned, dangerous group of Force-users who hold neither tradition. The Imperial assault still happens — they are not there for it. The protagonist hears about it from a comm transmission three weeks later. They will spend the rest of their life arguing with themselves about whether it was worth it. Some days the answer is yes. Some days it is no.
selection_signals: Malakai's offer accepted in Act 3 finale
high resistance to academy authority through Acts 1-2

the_law.name: The Law
the_law.synopsis: The protagonist brings Kira to Luke without warning her. Luke tries to be just. The trial is not clean. Kira is exiled from the academy with her training intact and her friendships ash. Malakai escapes with the academy intelligence Brakiss extracted. The Imperial Remnant uses it. The Praxeum holds, barely. The protagonist has done what the Order asked. They will not see Kira again for at least seven years. Luke does not say so directly, but he has clearly chosen to keep his distance from the protagonist after this.
selection_signals: high disposition with Luke maintained through Acts 2-3

the_long_road.name: The Long Road
the_long_road.synopsis: The protagonist refuses to bring Kira in but refuses to join Malakai. They give Kira three things and let her go: a stolen ship, a Karrde contact, and a promise to lie about where she is for as long as it takes. They lie to Luke. Luke knows. Luke does not press. The Imperial assault is met by the academy without the protagonist on the front line — the protagonist is somewhere else, doing something nobody at the academy is told about, that may or may not have changed how the assault unfolded. The protagonist returns four months later. Luke asks them no questions. Tionne does. Kam Solusar asks them only one.
selection_signals: mixed disposition signals — high with Kira, medium with Luke
Karrde information offer accepted in Act 4

what_remains.name: What Remains
what_remains.synopsis: The default ending. The protagonist did not commit cleanly to any of the four major paths and got carried by events. The Imperial assault comes. Kira makes her own choice without the protagonist's help. Some students survive. Some do not. Iila Vand is in the second group on most variants of this ending — the player did not earn the merciful version. The protagonist is alive, the academy is wounded, and the only person they are honest with about what happened is Kyp Durron, who knew this morning would come.
selection_signals: no clear branch commitment in Act 3
lie_grip oscillates without trend through campaign

era_voice.voice_notes:
The galaxy is breathing again, but unevenly. The New Republic governs the core; Imperial remnants and warlords fester on the rim. Luke Skywalker's Praxeum at Yavin 4 is rebuilding the Jedi tradition from scattered fragments — every student a potential heir, every misstep a chance to repeat history. The Exar Kun crisis is one year past; the ancient Sith Lord's spirit was banished by the unified will of the students, but the lower Massassi temples remain sealed and the older students still flinch at certain frequencies of stone. Kam Solusar is now an instructor. Kyp Durron is a Knight rebuilding what he broke. Streen lives in the high tower, eats alone, listens to the wind. Hope is fragile and named — and the Praxeum is learning that the cost of teaching the Force without the old Order is paid by the people who thought they were past their worst day.

TONE NOTE — this campaign is permitted, and encouraged, to be edgier than typical Jedi-Praxeum fiction. People the protagonist loves can die. The academy can fall. The antagonist's argument must be hard to refute. There is no clean ending. Specifically: do not soften violence into metaphor; do not soften betrayal into misunderstanding; do not soften moral compromise into regret-the-character-can-grow-from. The Order failed the galaxy and the Praxeum has not yet earned the trust the player is extending it. Honour that — not by being grim for its own sake, but by refusing the easy out.
period_details: Imperial remnants — warlord fleets, rogue Moffs, holdout Star Destroyers — still raid New Republic shipping

The Praxeum at Yavin 4 is a small academy built on rediscovered Jedi texts and Luke's instinct, expanded after the Exar Kun crisis with Kam Solusar (instructor), Cilghal (healer), and journeyman Knights like Kyp Durron and Dorsk 81
Force-sensitive recruits arrive from disparate paths — ex-Imperials, smuggler crews, war orphans, Mon Calamari refugees, even occasional Wookiee veterans of the Kashyyyk liberation
The lower Massassi temples beneath the Praxeum remain sealed; the vergence at the heart of them is quieted but not gone, and senior students remember Exar Kun's whispers in their ear
Surviving Inquisitors operate as freelancers, no longer answering to any unified Imperial command
Talon Karrde's information network is the closest thing the post-war fringe has to a clearing house; smugglers like the Glass Wake still trade through him
The New Republic Senate is debating whether the Jedi answer to civilian authority — a question Luke is quietly avoiding by training as fast as he can
period_avoid: First Order, Snoke, Kylo Ren, or any Sequel-era language
Empire as a galaxy-spanning intact regime — it is fragments and warlords now
Pre-Empire references that would only be known to Old Republic survivors
Treating the New Republic as a fully consolidated, peaceful authority
